scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Todd Anderson and I'm 31. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?
Okay, Todd. I see you're asking about a refund. Can you tell me your account number and the date you canceled the service?
My account number is 882910, and I canceled on October 1st. I'm really hoping you can make an exception since I was out of the country.
I already have your name and age from your first message, but I need you to confirm your email address on file so I can look at the account.
Look, our system shows the cancellation date was indeed 34 days ago. That's just our policy, we can't refund anything past 30 days. There is nothing I can do here.
I understand the policy, but as I said, I was traveling and unable to check my statements. Is there anyone else I can speak with to see if an exception can be made?
I guess I can send this to the billing department, but they usually just deny these anyway. I'll open a ticket for you.

escalation_reason: Customer insisted on an exception to the 30-day refund policy due to travel circumstances; agent lacked the authority or willingness to resolve.

judge_scores.justification: The agent verified the account details appropriately but demonstrated poor empathy by dismissing the customer's travel circumstances. The agent refused to make an effort within their authority and offered a defeatist attitude when finally agreeing to escalate the ticket.
